mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW Z3 2.2i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW Z3 2.2i engine replacement typically costs £1,400-£3,200 supply-only for rebuilt units, or £2,800-£4,800 fitted by a specialist. Used M54B22 engines: £1,100-£1,400 supply-only. Reconditioned units: £1,900-£2,300 supply-only. Rebuilt units with warranty: £2,200-£3,200 supply-only. Professional fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on workshop location.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW Z3 2.2i M54 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M54B22 is a robust engine when properly maintained, but it has well-documented weaknesses. VANOS seal degradation, CCV failure, and cooling system issues are the most common problems on higher-mileage examples. VANOS seals typically fail between 60,000-100,000 miles. CCV valve failure causes oil consumption and blue smoke. Cooling system components should be replaced preventatively at 80,000 miles. Regular oil changes (every 8,000-10,000 miles) significantly extend engine life.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of VANOS failure in a BMW Z3 2.2i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptoms are a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start, a noticeable loss of low-end power (the engine feels flat below 3,500rpm), rough idle, and decreased fuel economy. Cold-start rattle that disappears as the engine warms is the earliest warning sign. Loss of low-end torque and a 'flat' feel below 3,500rpm. Rough idle and occasional stalling. Specialist VANOS seal replacement costs £450-£750.

mainEntity.name: Why does my BMW Z3 2.2i burn oil?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oil consumption on the M54B22 is typically caused by CCV (crankcase ventilation) valve failure, worn valve stem seals, or a combination of both. CCV valve failure draws oil into the intake manifold. Valve stem seals harden with age, allowing oil past the valve guides. Blue smoke on start-up and excessive oil consumption (1L per 1,000 miles) are common signs. CCV replacement costs £300-£500 at a specialist.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a high-mileage BMW Z3 2.2i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Z3 2.2i worth £6,000-£14,000, a rebuilt M54B22 at £2,200-£3,200 can make financial sense if the body, interior, and rear subframe are in good condition. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to 70% of car's value. Sapphire and Titanium Edition examples command higher values and justify replacement. Classic car values are rising - a well-maintained Z3 2.2i is a sound investment. Always factor 12-month warranty into replacement decision.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M54B22 and the M52TUB22?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both engine codes refer to the same 2.2-litre straight-six engine fitted to the Z3. M52TUB22 was the earlier designation used in some parts catalogues and technical documentation, while M54B22 is the more common code used in UK vehicle registration data. Both are 2,171cc straight-six engines with dual-VANOS. M54B22 is the later, more commonly referenced engine code. Same power output (170hp), same torque (210Nm). Parts and rebuild costs are identical for both codes.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW Z3 2.2i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW Z3 2.2i was introduced as part of the E36/7 facelift in 2000, filling the gap between the entry-level four-cylinder models and the flagship 3.0i. Powered exclusively by the M54B22 2.2-litre straight-six, it offered the classic BMW inline-six experience - smooth, progressive power delivery with the characterful exhaust note enthusiasts expect - at a more accessible price point than the 3.0-litre variant.

milestones.description: M54B22 2.2-litre straight-six introduced in Z3 facelift, 170hp, 210Nm torque
Sapphire Edition and Titanium Edition special trims released, featuring M Sport suspension and cosmetic upgrades
Final year of Z3 2.2i production; replaced by the Z4 2.5i in the E85 generation
present - Z3 2.2i enters classic/enthusiast market; M54 engine maintenance and replacement demand persists

commonProblems.h2: BMW Z3 2.2i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW Z3 2.2i's M54B22 straight-six delivers the classic inline-six experience, but as these engines age beyond 80,000 miles, predictable wear patterns emerge - VANOS seal degradation, CCV failure, and cooling system weaknesses being the most common. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address these original failure points - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: VANOS Seal Failure - Why the BMW Z3 2.2i Loses Low-End Power
problems.rootCause: The dual-VANOS system uses rubber seals that degrade over time, losing hydraulic pressure and causing rattle on start-up, rough idle, and a noticeable loss of low-end torque - the engine feels flat below 3,500rpm.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace VANOS seals with upgraded Viton units, reset timing, full system test
repairOptions.longevity: Restores factory power delivery; 60,000+ mile lifespan

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M54B22 with upgraded VANOS, new seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if VANOS failure caused timing chain damage or if high mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW Z3 2.2i is worth £6,000-£14,000 for standard examples, with Sapphire and Titanium Editions commanding a premium. Given the vehicle's classic car value, engine replacement is generally viable even at the upper end of the cost range. For higher-mileage examples with other wear issues, evaluate the vehicle's overall condition - particularly the rear subframe mountings - before committing.
problems.recommendation: VANOS seal failure on the M54B22 is a well-understood issue. Specialist VANOS seal replacement using upgraded Viton seals costs under £750 and restores factory power delivery. This is almost always the right first step - a full engine replacement is rarely necessary unless the engine has suffered catastrophic failure or exceeded 150,000 miles with multiple other issues.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M54B22 engine prices for your BMW Z3 2.2i

problems.h4: CCV Failure - Why the BMW Z3 2.2i Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: The crankcase ventilation valve (CCV) diaphragm tears, allowing oil to be drawn into the intake manifold. Symptoms include excessive oil consumption (1L per 1,000 miles or more), blue smoke on start-up, and rough idle.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace CCV valve, all hoses, clean intake, oil change
repairOptions.longevity: Restores normal oil consumption; 60,000+ mile lifespan

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M54B22 with new CCV, valve stem seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil consumption has caused catalytic converter damage

problems.recommendation: CCV failure is one of the most common M54 issues and is relatively inexpensive to fix. At £300-£500 at a specialist, it's cheap insurance against catalytic converter damage. If you're seeing blue smoke on start-up but the car otherwise runs well, start with the CCV system before considering more expensive repairs.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW Z3 2.2i CCV repair and replacement

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the BMW Z3 2.2i Overheats
problems.rootCause: The M54 cooling system uses plastic components (expansion tank, water pump impeller, thermostat housing) that become brittle under repeated thermal cycling. Failure can cause sudden coolant loss and overheating - a warped aluminium cylinder head is the common consequence.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, hoses, coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Extends lifespan by 40,000+ miles if caught before overheating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head skim, pressure test, new head gasket, cooling system overhaul
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if block and bottom end remain undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M54B22 with upgraded cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating caused cracked block or scored bores

problems.recommendation: On any Z3 2.2i approaching 80,000 miles without documented cooling system work, proactive replacement of the water pump, thermostat, and expansion tank is the single best investment you can make. A £500-£850 specialist overhaul is far cheaper than a £2,200+ engine rebuild. Check coolant levels monthly and address any leaks immediately.
